title: Launch plan + beta customer selection for model metadata + automated release notes
creator: Marissa Cole
project: Model Metadata Schema v1 + Changelog Generator (Unified Rollouts)
description:
Objective
- Define the beta customer cohort and execution plan for GA launch of: (1) model metadata schema v1 adoption, (2) automated customer-visible release notes (Console + docs), and (3) internal audit/change visibility for support and compliance.

Why this matters
- Enterprise and regulated prospects are explicitly blocking on customer-visible model change history + release notes + auditability (see Northbridge security review, Lattice deep dive, SUP-28429 output regression after silent change).
- We need a controlled rollout to validate public vs internal separation, redaction rules, and support workflows before broad enablement.

Scope of this PM ticket
- Beta customer selection criteria + candidate list
- External comms plan for beta and GA (what we say, what we do not say)
- Support/CS readiness plan (playbooks, escalation, RBAC access, interim exports)
- Success metrics + launch gates (ship/hold)
- Timeline coordination across Product/Eng/Docs/Security

Out of scope
- Implementations in code (tracked in ENG tickets)
- Full customer notification subscriptions (email/webhook) beyond any basic internal webhook plumbing

Beta principle
- The beta must include at least one regulated org (audit requirements) and at least one fast-moving product org (high release cadence), across at least two deployment modes.

Candidate customers (initial)
- Northbridge Capital Markets (Private/VPC interest; strict audit/retention; procurement blocker: change visibility)
- Lattice Health Systems (Dedicated evaluation; wants rollout policies + rollback guidance)
- 1–2 additional smaller accounts with high Hosted usage and frequent model pinning/version discussions (to be proposed by CS)

Proposed rollout phases
1) Internal dogfood (Redwood apps + internal tenants)
   - Ensure Console never renders internal-only notes to non-admin roles (regression tested)
   - Validate release-note generation coverage for model promotions + metadata edits
2) Limited beta (2–4 customers)
   - Enable release notes feed in Console for selected tenants
   - Provide docs release notes pages for beta (public pages may still be limited to a beta flag / non-indexed)
   - Support + CS have playbooks + internal audit view access
3) GA (all tenants)
   - Publish public docs release notes pages + stable RSS/JSON feed
   - Announce in changelog + (optional) targeted customer comms

Key decisions needed in this ticket
- Beta gating mechanism (feature flag by org/tenant vs by deployment mode)
- “Public vs internal” comms: which quality/perf statements are allowed and required approval path
- Support access model: who gets internal audit views (Support/TAMs) and how access is requested/approved

Proposed deliverables from this ticket
- Beta cohort proposal + confirmation from CS/AE owners
- Beta enablement checklist + execution timeline
- Customer comms templates (beta invite, beta onboarding note, known limitations, feedback channel)
- Support/CS readiness checklist + runbook links
- Launch gates (GO/NO-GO) and success metrics definition
acceptance_criteria: Beta cohort list finalized (2–4 customers) with owner, deployment mode, and risk profile; approvals from Product + CS + Security where applicable
Written beta comms package: invite email copy, beta onboarding steps, expectations + limitations, escalation path, feedback channel
Support readiness complete: internal RBAC access process + support playbook for ‘customer reports output drift after model update’ (what to check, where to find history, what to share)
Launch gates defined and agreed: public/internal redaction correctness, release note generation coverage %, rollback story for a bad promotion, docs publishing safety check
Success metrics defined with measurement plan (dashboards or reports identified) and beta exit criteria set
GA announcement plan drafted (docs + Console surfaces + optional changelog post) with clear wording aligned to style guide
success_metrics: Release note coverage: >= 95% of model version promotions in beta have customer-visible release notes within 30 minutes of promotion event
Redaction correctness: 0 instances of internal-only fields visible to non-admin users in beta (validated by automated tests + manual spot checks)
Support efficiency: median time-to-identify ‘what changed’ in a model regression ticket reduced by 50% (baseline from SUP-28429 investigation notes)
Customer feedback: >= 2 beta customers confirm the new change history/release notes meets their change visibility requirements (documented in notes)
Reliability: docs build publishes complete notes only (no incomplete/empty artifacts); 0 repeat of prior incomplete release note incident in beta
beta_selection_criteria: Has expressed a need for model change visibility / release notes / auditability (explicit requirement or recent escalations)
Uses at least one of: version pinning, canary/A-B rollouts, Dedicated capacity tuning, or Private upgrade bundles
Willing to give feedback on note clarity and operational expectations within 2 weeks of enablement
Has identified technical owner + CS/TAM owner for quick turnaround on feedback and incident response
Includes at least one regulated/compliance-heavy org (audit, retention, access controls) and one fast-iteration org (high cadence, developer-driven)
Represents at least two deployment modes across the cohort (Hosted + Dedicated and/or Private)
comms_plan: Beta invite (email + short enablement doc): what’s included (Console release notes + per-model history), what’s not (notifications, full historical backfill), and how to provide feedback
Beta onboarding call agenda: confirm deployment mode + access controls, show where to view release notes/history, confirm what data is public vs internal, establish escalation contacts
In-product messaging: ‘Beta’ badge in Console release notes view with link to feedback form and known limitations
GA comms: update public docs release notes landing page + add Console tooltip/FAQ; optional ‘What’s new’ entry in Redwood changelog

Wording constraints: quality/perf claims must follow taxonomy/style guide; no over-claims without statistically significant evidence; no internal incident references; no infrastructure vendor details; no customer-specific identifiers
support_cs_readiness_plan: RBAC: Support/CS access to internal-only change/audit views via approved group + audit trail (ties to INT-11903 and ENG-9828 outcomes)

Runbook: ‘Customer reports output change’ triage steps (confirm model/version, check change history, look for rollout phase, validate region/deployment differences, gather prompts/evidence, consult eval tags)
Interim export option: if Console UI is delayed, provide internal export endpoint/report for per-model recent changes (for TAMs/support) with strict redaction
Escalation matrix: Support -> TAM -> Eng on-call (Console/Control Plane) with severity guidelines; security escalation if redaction breach suspected
Customer-facing FAQ draft reviewed and ready to share (coordinate with CS draft FAQ in Drive)
launch_gates: Public vs internal redaction rules validated end-to-end (API -> Console -> docs build) including regression test coverage for the prior internal-notes rendering bug
Docs publishing guardrails: build fails if release note artifact is empty/incomplete; staging preview required for any template changes
Eventing correctness: promotion + metadata edit events generate deterministic changelog entries (idempotent ingestion; no duplicates) for beta tenants
Rollback story proven: for a promoted model version, release note can be amended with ‘rolled back’ entry and Console shows the rollback clearly
Support playbooks approved by Dev Patel + Liam O'Rourke; internal access workflow documented and tested
Security sign-off: audit event retention and SIEM export expectations documented for beta (esp. Private)
timeline: 2025-10-11 to 2025-10-15: finalize beta criteria + candidate list; confirm willingness and technical owners
2025-10-16 to 2025-10-20: internal dogfood + support training; verify redaction + docs publishing gates
2025-10-21: enable beta cohort (feature flag) + run onboarding calls
2025-10-22 to 2025-10-29: beta observation window; weekly feedback sync; iterate on wording/templates
2025-10-30: beta exit review + GA GO/NO-GO decision; finalize GA comms
2025-11-03 week: GA rollout staged (10% -> 50% -> 100%) depending on incident rate and support load
open_questions: Do we want beta docs release notes pages to be publicly accessible but non-indexed, or fully gated behind auth during beta?
What is the minimum acceptable ‘backfill’ for beta customers (e.g., last 30 days of promotions only)?
Do we require customer approval before adding any mention of their participation in the beta (default: yes, do not mention publicly)?
How do we handle region-staggered rollouts in release notes phrasing without confusing customers?
What’s the threshold for calling something a ‘breaking change’ in model behavior vs ‘behavioral change’ per the style guide?
updates: 2025-10-12 (Talia Benson): Drafted beta criteria + initial cohort (Northbridge, Lattice). Requested CS to propose 1–2 high-cadence Hosted customers for contrast; waiting on Miguel/Dev inputs.

2025-10-14 (Paula Mendes): Requested explicit rollout-policy validation during beta: ensure release notes surface ‘rollout eligibility’ and show when a version is in canary vs fully promoted for a tenant.

2025-10-16 (Marissa Cole): Confirmed with Sales that Northbridge is willing to pilot provided audit events + retention posture is documented. Need Security review of what we can claim publicly about audit logs in release notes UI/FAQ.
2025-10-18 (Talia Benson): Added launch gates around docs build completeness due to prior incomplete release note incident. Scheduled support enablement session for 2025-10-22 pending Eng readiness.
comments: Dylan Brooks (2025-10-13): Please make sure beta plan explicitly calls out a rollback demo. We’ve had customers assume ‘release notes exist’ means ‘no changes without notes’—we need clarity on version pinning vs default alias behavior.

Dev Patel (2025-10-14): Support needs a single place to answer ‘what changed for customer X’ even if the change is internal-only. If Console UI isn’t ready, we need an internal export (CSV/JSON) with org filter and timestamps.

Naomi Feldman (2025-10-16): For regulated prospects, be careful with retention promises. We can describe audit event types and access controls, but any retention window should be tied to contract tier / deployment mode.

Elliot Price (2025-10-17): Docs team can publish beta pages, but we need a clear IA/URL plan and whether pages are public or authenticated. Also we should add a warning banner for ‘beta notes may update as rollout progresses.’
